text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- "Terrorists" kill four policemen in three attacks in Algiers.
- Political parties step up preparations ahead of the election campaign in mid-May.
- President Liamine Zeroual pays a two-day visit to the southern town of Ghardaia to oversee development programmes.

- Francisco Cobos Flores, head of the U.N. observers to monitor the June 5 general elections in Algeria, meets Salah Boubnider, chief of a local multi-party poll watchdog, to coordinate the works of the two bodies.
- About 8,000 candidates stand for the parliamentary elections. More than 47 percent are aged below 40 and about half of them are university graduates.

- Algeria's Foreign Minister Ahmed Attaf says Algeria is awaiting U.N envoy James Baker's proposals on the Western Sahara conflict. Baker visited the region in April to tackle a stalled U.N.-sponsored peace process.
- Algerian workers celebrated May Day demanding more pay increases.
